subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should the sandbox cold-start mitigation default to bounded fail-soft Docker control-plane timeouts now, wait for live macOS/OrbStack isolation first, or be narrowed to the linked wedged-Docker issue only?
rationale: The source-level no-timeout gap is real, but the reported intermittent cold-start window spans several sandbox-prep substeps and the timeout/default behavior can change existing slow-Docker operator expectations.

options.title: Refresh timeout/fail-soft path
options.body: Review or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91015 so it bounds the full Docker control-plane path, preserves current main behavior, documents the default/config boundary, and includes real macOS/OrbStack proof.

options.title: Require diagnostics first
options.body: Keep this issue open for reporter logs or a live repro that isolates whether prune, workspace layout, Docker user resolution, or backend creation owns the 30+ minute wait before choosing a fix.

options.title: Close after narrower fix lands
options.body: If the linked wedged-Docker fix or successor demonstrably covers the observed cold-start stalls, close this issue after the merged implementation and release/main provenance are available.

recommendation.title: Refresh timeout/fail-soft path
recommendation.body: Review or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91015 so it bounds the full Docker control-plane path, preserves current main behavior, documents the default/config boundary, and includes real macOS/OrbStack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox architecture, prune/runtime cleanup, and compatibility-sensitive default behavior where available history shows repeated work.
